subject: AuroraEdge on-prem: PVC binding strategy & node failure-slice plan
messages:
From: Tom Harris <tom.harris@auroraedge.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lucy Chen <lucy.chen@auroraedge.com>
Date: 2028-02-10T10:23:00-05:00
Subject: AuroraEdge on-prem: PVC binding strategy & node failure-slice plan

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking this. We're moving from an SRE-led prototype to a regulated on-prem rollout and need to lock down how Redwood will be deployed inside our co-lo. Primary asks:

- PVC placement strategy for mixed NVMe/SSD tiers (hot vs warm workloads)
- Node slice approach so inference pods survive single-disk and single-host failures without overprovisioning GPUs
- How to ensure predictable latency when prefix caching is enabled across multiple failure domains

Quick context: 6 racks, 12 GPU hosts (A100s, 4 GPUs each), 8 storage hosts (NVMe local + shared NFS for backups). Expected 99th p99 token latency target < 250ms for 75% of requests, with warm-batching for batch tasks.

I've attached a short ops checklist and the cluster inventory CSV for your review. Can we do a 30-minute sync early next week?

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Harris
Head of Platform Engineering, AuroraEdge
(Attachment: initial-ops-checklist.pdf)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@auroraedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-10T14:07:00-05:00
Subject: Re: AuroraEdge on-prem: PVC binding strategy & node failure-slice plan

Tom — thanks, got the checklist and inventory. I skimmed the CSV; helpful. Quick answers and next steps below, then I'll loop in Marissa for PV-class specifics and Priyom for rollout runbook items.

High-level approach (preview):
- PVC binding: recommend mix of nodeAffinity + storageClass topologyBinding for hot NVMe PVs (local persistent volumes) and RWO NFS-backed classes for warm/backup data. Avoid RWX for inference caches to reduce cross-host network jitter.
- Node slices: propose 3 logical slices per rack — inference-primary (GPU-heavy), inference-eviction-safe (lower-priority pods that can be preempted), and infra (control-plane + monitoring). Use PodDisruptionBudgets and static admission quotas per slice to ensure at least 1 GPU stays available per rack.
- Latency with prefix caching: cache-local-first with LRU eviction; we suggest co-locating cache volumes on the same NVMe host as the inference GPU when possible and adding a small KV-replicated fallback on the NFS tier. This reduces cross-host reads and keeps p99 down.

Questions (before the sync):
1) Are NVMe devices presented as local PVs or via a block abstraction (LVM)?
2) Which OS and k8s distro (we saw "k8s-1.28" in the CSV but confirm control-plane HA model)?
3) Do you have a preferred backup cadence for model artifacts (daily vs hourly)?

Proposed next step: 30-min call Mon 2028-02-13 09:30 PT. If that works I'll circulate an agenda and Marissa will attach the PV-class matrix.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: auroraedge-cluster-inventory.csv)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@auroraedge.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-13T08:02:00-05:00
Subject: Re: AuroraEdge on-prem: PVC binding strategy & node failure-slice plan

Tom / team — added a short PV-class matrix and rationale (see attached pv-class-matrix.xlsx). Topline recommendations from an ops perspective:

- storage-class-hot-nvme (local PV, volumeMode: Block, topology: "kubernetes.io/hostname") — for model weights and prefix caches. Use volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer to ensure pod scheduled on the host with NVMe.
- storage-class-warm-ssd (RWO via LVM on SSD hosts) — for checkpointing and less latency-sensitive artifacts.
- storage-class-archive-nfs (RWX) — for backups and long-term logs; cheaper and cross-host.

PV sizing guidance: keep cache PVs thin-provisioned with a target local hit-rate 85% (we provide tooling in Redwood Optimize to measure this). For failure tolerance, use kube-scheduler topologySpreadConstraints + soft-affinity so pods prefer different hosts but can colocate if resources are tight.

I've also modeled two slicing options in the spreadsheet: conservative (reserve 1 GPU per rack for high-priority traffic) and elastic (allow burst eviction with preemption). We should choose based on SLO strictness; given your p99 target I'd recommend conservative for first 90 days.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: pv-class-matrix.xlsx)

From: Tom Harris <tom.harris@auroraedge.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lucy Chen <lucy.chen@auroraedge.com>
Date: 2028-02-14T11:46:00-05:00
Subject: Re: AuroraEdge on-prem: PVC binding strategy & node failure-slice plan

Thanks — this is exactly the level we needed. Quick clarifications:

- NVMe is presented via LVM stripe on each host (so not simple block passthrough).
- k8s distro is kOps 1.28 with 3 control-plane VMs (HA)
- Backup cadence: artifacts hourly (for model rollbacks) and daily cold backups to NFS.

Given the LVM detail, does the recommendation change for volumeMode=Block vs Filesystem for our hot caches? We're aiming for minimal serialization overhead. Also, curious about the trade-off you mentioned between conservative vs elastic slicing — how long to run conservative before moving to elastic?

Happy to keep the 2/13 call as a recorded sync for our CTO if you want — otherwise can push to the 15th.

Tom

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@auroraedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-16T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Re: AuroraEdge on-prem: PVC binding strategy & node failure-slice plan

Tom — short answers and an action plan.

1) LVM-backed NVMe: keep volumeMode=Filesystem for caches if you need POSIX semantics (easier for our runtime). If raw throughput is the only concern and your caching layer supports direct block devices, consider Block mode with a small FIO benchmark (we can run this in your lab). Marissa: can you add a short perf note to the PV matrix about LVM+Block vs FS?
2) Conservative -> Elastic cadence: run conservative slicing for the initial 8–12 weeks (collect p99 telemetry and cache-hit metrics). If p99 consistently < 200ms and cache-hit >= 85% with headroom on GPU utilization, we can transition to elastic with staged canaries. Priyom will be owner for the rollout gating.

Action items:
- Marissa to add LVM perf note to pv-class-matrix.xlsx (by 2028-02-18).
- Priyom to draft a 6-week conservative rollout runbook (OPS-3249) and gate criteria (by 2028-02-20).
- Mina to schedule a recorded design review with AuroraEdge on 2028-02-21 09:30 PT and share the recording and slides.

Links: HubSpot deal RDW-2028-AUR-47 (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890) and Jira runbook OPS-3249 (https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/OPS-3249).
